title: Send · empty
desc: First impression and the most-used screen. One giant paste target; nothing to decide until there’s content.

title: Send · filled
desc: Content was pasted; Cryptex split it into fields. The policy is one line with sensible defaults.

title: Send · options
desc: The policy line expands in place. Every option is a real control with a one-line consequence.

title: Send · encrypting
desc: Large files encrypt in chunks in the browser, then upload. Progress is per file and resumable.

title: Send · link ready
desc: After Create, the link is already on the clipboard. The page becomes the receipt; no separate share step.

title: Your links
desc: The sender’s home after the first send. Sorted by who has to act; the one item that needs you is tinted.

title: Receipt
desc: One item’s history. Times only, never contents. The warning gives the next step if the timing looks wrong.

title: Request · new
desc: Same composer, pointed the other way. Fields are suggested from the title; everything is optional except the title.

title: Request · link ready
desc: Mirror of the send result. Explains where the private key lives and offers a backup link.

title: Respond to a request
desc: What the person asked sees. A plain form with exactly the requested fields, branded as the company asking.

title: Respond · sent
desc: Closure for the responder, plus a gentle path to becoming a sender.

title: Reveal · sealed
desc: Nothing happens on load. The security-tint top is the “still sealed” signal; it disappears once revealed.

title: Reveal · confirm email
desc: Shown when the sender limited the secret to one email. The code check happens before any encrypted data is sent.

title: Reveal · passphrase
desc: Wrong-passphrase state. Tries are limited so a leaked link plus guessing can’t work.

title: Revealed
desc: Values stay masked until asked for, copy one at a time, and the page clears itself after 5 idle minutes.

title: Reveal · already opened
desc: The most common confusing moment, explained with a time and a next step. Same layout for “expired”.

title: Reveal · incomplete link
desc: Truncated links are a real failure mode with fragment keys. Detect a short key client-side before calling the server.

title: Server · overview
desc: Is the server healthy, and is anything misconfigured? No list of other people’s secrets.

title: Server · access
desc: Replaces public/private mode and the shared admin password with sign-in and named owners.

title: Server · limits
desc: Inline validation with the server’s own parsers. Env-controlled values are locked and say why.

title: Server · branding
desc: White-label for the company running the server. The live preview uses the real recipient components.

title: Server · notifications
desc: SMTP and webhooks in one place, with a test button and clear consequences when off.

title: Server · API tokens
desc: Tokens are personal and scoped. The CLI encrypts locally, like the browser.

title: Server · audit log
desc: What security reviewers ask for. Events only: who, what, when, which link ID.

title: First-run setup
desc: Replaces the default admin/admin. The server refuses to create links until step 1 is done.

title: Sign in
desc: SSO first; password only for owners. Says clearly that recipients never need this page.

title: Demo · send
desc: Same app, fixed limits, honest banner on every page (recipient pages too). No sign-in, no Server writes.

title: Demo · limit reached
desc: Rate-limit state. States the reset time, keeps sent links working, and turns the limit into an install path.

title: Destroy confirmation
desc: The only confirm in the send flow. Focus starts on “Keep it”; Escape closes. On phones it’s a bottom sheet.

title: QR code
desc: For handing a secret across a desk. The QR is drawn locally from the full link; nothing is sent anywhere.

title: Upload failed
desc: Network or server failure during create. The content is never lost and the error says what happened.

title: Your links · empty
desc: First visit to Your links. Explains the page and offers both directions.

title: Account menu
desc: The avatar opens this menu: navigation that doesn’t fit on phones, the theme setting, and sign out. On phones it’s a bottom sheet.

title: Page not found
desc: 404 and 500 pages. They never reveal whether a secret ID exists.

title: API token created
desc: Show-once secret with an explicit acknowledgement. Tokens expire by default.

title: Components
desc: Every building block on one page, in both themes, for the developer building the component library.
